title: Protocol for Incomplete Murine Tumor Resection to Study Local Effects of Surgical Trauma
author: McCaw, Dao, et al.
materials: Use hemostat to develop subcutaneous plane.

steps.title: Prepare skin preparation area
steps.instruction: Set up the skin preparation area (≈5 min) by laying an absorbent under‑pad over the prep area, placing a heating pad underneath, turning it on and confirming the surgical field is at an appropriate temperature by touch. Arrange 10 % betadine solution and 70 % ethanol in silver trays with 2 × 2 in gauze, provide eye‑lubrication Q‑tips, and position a nosecone on the absorbent pad for continued anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Lay absorbent under‑pad over prep area.
Place heating pad under absorbent pad, turn on, verify temperature.
Place 10 % betadine solution and 70 % ethanol at edge of area with 2 × 2 in gauze.
Provide eye‑lubrication and Q‑tips.
Place nosecone on absorbent pad for anesthesia.

steps.title: Connect anesthesia tubing
steps.instruction: Connect tubing from the oxygen tank to the isoflurane vaporizer, induction chamber, preparation‑area nosecone, and charcoal canister using a Y‑splitter and diverter valves; one splitter outlet goes to the induction chamber, the other to the nosecone, and the charcoal canister attaches to the induction chamber to scavenge isoflurane.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia in mouse
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in the induction chamber, start isoflurane flow, and once the mouse is unresponsive, transfer it onto the absorbent pad with its face in the nosecone.

steps.title: Apply eye lubrication
steps.instruction: Apply liberal eye lubrication to each eye using a Q‑tip.

steps.title: Prepare operative skin site
steps.instruction: Coat the operative site and flank with betadine‑soaked 2 × 2 in gauze, starting at the site and moving outward in a circular fashion; repeat this three times using fresh gauze each time. Then coat the same area with ethanol‑soaked 2 × 2 in gauze in the same outward circular manner, also repeating three times with fresh gauze.

substeps.instruction: Betadine soak gauze, coat site, outward circular motion, repeat 3× with new gauze.
Ethanol soak gauze, coat site, outward circular motion, repeat 3× with new gauze.

steps.title: Transfer mouse to surgical field
steps.instruction: Assistant gently picks up the mouse by foreleg and tail, places it with the prepared operative site facing up, and positions it directly in front of the nosecone, taking care not to touch the sterile field.

steps.title: Start nosecone anesthesia
steps.instruction: Begin flow of isoflurane to the nosecone in the surgical field.

steps.title: Remove excess prep fluid
steps.instruction: Using a dry 2 × 2 in gauze, remove any excess betadine/ethanol fluid from the mouse to avoid heat loss from vaporization (skip this step if chlorhexidine‑based prep was used).

steps.title: Confirm anesthesia depth
steps.instruction: Perform a toe‑pinch; absence of withdrawal indicates adequate anesthesia. Periodically monitor breathing rate—fewer, larger breaths indicate appropriate depth.

steps.title: Make flank incision
steps.instruction: Using a #15 blade, make a 2 cm incision over the flank, planning it 5–10 mm dorsal to the tumor. Press and spread the skin of the upper abdomen/flank with the non‑dominant hand’s index finger and thumb (avoid direct pressure on the tumor), cut the incision, and deepen it full‑thickness until pink/red muscle is visible; use scissors if needed to achieve full thickness.

substeps.instruction: Plan incision 5–10 mm dorsal to tumor.
Stretch skin with non‑dominant hand, avoiding tumor.
Make 2 cm incision with #15 blade.
Deepen incision full‑thickness to expose underlying muscle.

steps.title: Develop subcutaneous plane
steps.instruction: With Adson forceps in the non‑dominant hand, lift the skin edge on the tumor side; slide a closed hemostat forward under the skin perpendicular to underlying tissue, spreading it slowly (tines 1–1.5 cm apart) so the skin pulls away, then withdraw the hemostat open. Repeat several times until the tumor and surrounding area are adequately exposed; cut any thin avascular adhesive bands sparingly if they form.

steps.title: Evert skin to expose tumor
steps.instruction: Using the non‑dominant hand’s index finger and thumb, grasp the cut skin edge on the tumor side and evert it so the tumor lies directly over the pad of the index finger and is easily palpable. Avoid excessive upward pressure that could rupture the tumor capsule.

steps.title: Perform incomplete tumor resection
steps.instruction: Using a #11 blade, transect the tumor, leaving approximately 50 % (or the desired residual amount) in place. First cut the tumor surface, then deepen the cut through the tumor body without violating the dermis, orienting the cut so the half distal to the draining (inguinal) lymph node is removed. Inspect for large feeding vessels; if present, pass a 4‑0 vicryl suture under the vessel with a Castroviejo needle holder, tie tightly, cut tails, and transect the vessel on the tumor side. Circumferentially release connective tissue around the portion to be removed starting 1–2 mm from the tumor edge, using the blade body parallel to the dermis to develop a plane between connective tissue and dermis. Continue the plane under the tumor until the initial bisecting cut is reached, taking care not to enter the dermis. Once freed, remove the tumor half with curved forceps, inspect the site, repeat connective‑tissue release if residual tumor remains, and control any bleeding with light pressure using 2 × 2 in gauze.

substeps.instruction: Cut tumor surface, leaving ~50 % residual.
Deepen cut through tumor body, avoid dermis.
Tie off large vessels with 4‑0 vicryl via Castroviejo holder, then transect vessel.
Release connective tissue 1–2 mm from tumor edge with #11 tip.
Develop plane parallel to dermis with blade body, 1–2 mm from edge.
Continue plane to bisecting cut, avoid dermis entry.
Remove tumor half with curved forceps.
Inspect site; repeat release steps if tumor remains.
Control bleeding with 2 × 2 in gauze.

steps.title: Optional inguinal lymph node removal
steps.instruction: Develop the subcutaneous plane toward the hind leg using Adson forceps and hemostat as before, expose the adipose tissue, locate the inguinal lymph node within the fat pad, dissect adjacent fatty tissue with pointed curved forceps, and remove the node with gentle traction while minimizing tissue trauma.

steps.title: Optional axillary lymph node removal
steps.instruction: Develop the subcutaneous plane toward the foreleg using Adson forceps and hemostat as before, expose the adipose tissue adjacent to the front leg, locate the axillary lymph node within the fat pad, dissect surrounding fatty tissue with pointed curved forceps, and remove the node with gentle traction, avoiding extensive trauma.

steps.title: Optional sham surgery
steps.instruction: On the contralateral flank, make an incision identical in length to the experimental incision, develop the subcutaneous plane as described in steps 22–23, and keep the mouse under anesthesia for the same duration as the incomplete‑resection group.

steps.title: Close surgical incision
steps.instruction: Load 4‑0 vicryl on a tapered needle into a Castroviejo needle holder. Using a buried deep‑dermal technique, pick up one skin edge with an Adson pick‑up (non‑dominant hand), pass the needle superficially through a small amount of dermis (not full thickness) on that side (deep‑to‑superficial orientation), reload, grasp the opposite skin edge, and pass the needle superficially through a small amount of dermis on that side (superficial‑to‑deep orientation). Pull the suture to the desired length, tie with 3–4 throws, cut leaving 1–2 mm tails, and gently pull the incision edges so the knot “pops” under the skin and is buried. Place successive sutures every 4–5 mm along the incision, then inspect to ensure the skin edges are well‑approximated.

substeps.instruction: Load 4‑0 vicryl on tapered needle into Castroviejo holder.
Pick up one skin edge with Adson pick‑up.
Pass needle superficially through small dermal bite (deep‑to‑superficial).
Reload, grasp opposite skin edge, pass needle superficially (superficial‑to‑deep).
Pull suture, tie with 3–4 throws, cut tails (1–2 mm).
Pull edges so knot buries under skin.
Repeat sutures every 4–5 mm.
Inspect incision for proper approximation.

steps.title: Transport mouse to recovery
steps.instruction: Surgeon picks up the mouse directly over the closed incision, using index finger and thumb to grasp skin on either side of the incision without tension, avoiding direct contact with the tumor. If gloves become contaminated, remove and don new sterile gloves.

steps.title: Proceed to next mouse
steps.instruction: Continue with the next mouse surgery; sterile gloves need not be changed between mice unless a breach occurs. If any tool contacts a non‑sterile surface or tissue, replace the tool or re‑sterilize it using a glass‑bead sterilizer.

steps.title: Standardize anesthesia for all cohorts
steps.instruction: Place mice in the no‑surgery cohort in the isoflurane induction chamber for a period equal to the average time per mouse surgery to ensure identical anesthesia and analgesia exposure across no‑surgery, sham, and incomplete‑resection groups.
